old_findings.note: the EIP-1271 calldata copy is still a word loop with the decimal selector 371636862 and a raw-memory staticcall, and its bound is now `_47 - _53 + ceil32(signature.length)` instead of `_56`, with the pad write `mem[2 * _47 - _53 + 2 * Mask(250, 5, signature.length + 31) + 32] = 0` (365-374).

regressions.decompiled: if _68: allowance[owner][spender] = amount ; _71 = mem[64] ; mem[mem[64]] = amount ; log Approval(..., uint256 value=mem[mem[64] len _71 - mem[64] + 32]) ; stop / _73 = mem[64] ; mem[mem[64]] = 0x08c379a0... ; mem[_73 + 4] = 32 ; mem[_73 + 36] = 18 ; mem[_73 + 68] = 0x536b792f... ; revert with memory from mem[64] len _73 - mem[64] + 100
regressions.old: if not _68: revert with 'Sky/invalid-permit' ; allowance[owner][spender] = amount ; log Approval(address indexed owner=owner, address indexed spender=spender, uint256 value=amount)
regressions.source: Sky.sol permit(..., bytes signature): require(_isValidSignature(owner, digest, signature), "Sky/invalid-permit"); allowance[owner][spender] = value; emit Approval(owner, spender, value)
regressions.issue: After the join of `if not return_data.size` (the returndata allocation now writes mem[64] in one arm), the decompiler no longer folds `v - mem[64]` for `v = mem[64]`, so the require message prints as a hand-built Error(string) buffer with a raw `revert with memory` and the Approval value as a memory range. Equivalent (lengths 100 and 32), much harder to read.
regressions.rule: A variable bound to mem[64] equals mem[64] until mem[64] itself is written (writes at mem[64] + k, k >= 32, never are), also after a join where mem[64] was a phi; fold `v - mem[64]` to 0 and decode Error(string) and log data on that base.

regressions.old: _13 = sha3(mem[_11 + 32 len mem[_11]]) ; signer = ecrecover(_13, ...) ; mem[_7 + 390] = _13
regressions.issue: `_7` and `_8` are two reads of mem[64] with no write to it between, so `_7 - _8` is 0 and the digest is `sha3(Bytes(2, 0x1901), _6, structHash)`; the text leaves the subtraction and now inlines the raw-memory hash 3 times per overload instead of one variable. The struct hash itself did improve (decoded).
regressions.rule: Fold the difference of two reads of mem[64] with no write to mem[64] between to 0; a hash of memory whose words are known prints as sha3 of those words.

improvements: The permit struct hash is decoded in both overloads (`sha3(PERMIT_TYPEHASH, owner, spender, value, nonce, deadline)`); hex padding (P6 gone).
notes: Whole diff read (145 lines, the two permit overloads). All changes stem from the free-memory-pointer rewrite: one helped (struct hash), the others left `v - mem[64]` / `_7 - _8` unfolded. The v,r,s permit keeps its clean `revert with 'Sky/invalid-permit'` and Approval tail. No semantic change: the same checks, writes, call, event and reverts in the same order.
summary: One medium regression: permit(bytes)'s 'Sky/invalid-permit' revert and Approval value now print as raw free-memory buffers; the EIP-712 digest and the EIP-1271 copy also got more obscure. Only the struct hash improved.
